title: Cauliflower: modeled ₹412/qtl left, Kangra (Baijnath) → Shimla
summary: March 2022: reported cauliflower prices at Kangra (Baijnath) and Shimla imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 91% of 23 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹412 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 1,334 same-variety market pairs screened for cauliflower in March 2022; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) at both markets; sale matched to the first Shimla report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: March 2022
scenes.caption: Kangra (Baijnath) (Himachal Pradesh) and Shimla (Himachal Pradesh) both reported cauliflower prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) on 23 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Kangra (Baijnath) reported a median ₹1,400 per quintal. Shimla reported a median ₹2,100 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹725/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹725 per quintal, and Shimla was dearer on 96% of days.

scenes.headline: 214 km by road
scenes.caption: 214 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~4 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹46/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹475 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹388 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Shimla report, the rule selects 17 of 23 modeled shipping days. 15 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹412 per quintal (₹297 under stress).

scenes.headline: The back-test
scenes.caption: The modeled Cauliflower route from Kangra (Baijnath) to Shimla was positive on 91% of matched days in March 2022. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹41,200, or ₹29,700 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

assumptions.value: onion survey freight applied per quintal to cauliflower
scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹46/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days
~450 road km a day → 1 days here

conclusion: The modeled Cauliflower route from Kangra (Baijnath) to Shimla was positive on 91% of matched days in March 2022. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹41,200, or ₹29,700 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.
